wave_title: Data Flow -- materialize the DATA_FLOW dimension (.atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-FACTS.md#dataflowfact, .atlas/roadmap/SELF-BUILDING-R4-R8.md R4.7): values; definitions/uses; parameter flow; return flow; load/store relationships; local propagation; typed unresolved/alias ambiguity where deeper analysis is unavailable. Reuses R4.6's key design insight: which lexical binding a bare identifier refers to within one function body is fully determined by Rust's own scoping/shadowing rules -- syntax alone, no type inference needed -- so this wave resolves it for real via a scope stack, unlike R4.5's CALL (which genuinely requires type/import resolution this extractor doesn't have). Deliberately bounded: only simple `Pat::Ident` bindings are modeled (tuple/struct destructuring stays Unresolved, not silently dropped); only plain `=` assignment produces a Store; alias/borrow/points-to analysis is explicitly out of scope.

data_flow_model.kernel: core/src/semantic/data_flow.rs: ValueRole (Definition/Use/Store), DataFlowResolution (Resolved/Unresolved), ValueIdentity { repository, revision, function, name, span, role, is_parameter, is_return_flow, resolution, resolved_definition }.
data_flow_model.identity_key_design: ValueIdentity::identity_key() covers repository/revision/function/name/span/role -- role participates because Definition/Use/Store are different entity kinds even at an identical (function, name, span) triple, unlike R4.6's ControlFlowBlockKind (purely descriptive content, since block_index alone already disambiguates). resolution/resolved_definition/is_parameter/is_return_flow are deliberately excluded: they are resolution facts about an already-identified entity that a later wave may compute more precisely for the exact same claim, not identity-distinguishing fields. Confirmed both by a core-level unit test and by independent falsification (removing `role` from the format string broke exactly identity_key_distinguishes_role, 75/76 passing).
data_flow_model.key_design_difference_from_call: Unlike R4.5's CALL (callee resolution genuinely requires name/type information this extractor doesn't have), which lexical binding a bare identifier resolves to within one function body is fully determined by Rust's own scoping/shadowing rules -- syntax alone. So, as with R4.6's CFG, real resolution is computed via a scope stack rather than left Unresolved by default; Unresolved is reserved for genuinely undeterminable cases (no matching local definition -- a field access, module item, or closure capture from an enclosing scope).
data_flow_model.extraction: adapter/src/semantic/rust/dataflow.rs (new file): DataFlowWalker tracks a scope_stack: Vec<BTreeMap<String, SemanticRecordId>>, one map per open lexical block/pattern scope, pushed/popped around function bodies, if/loop/for bodies, and match arms. Parameters (including &self) are bound as Definitions in an outer scope before the body is walked. simple_pat_ident recognizes only Pat::Ident (through Pat::Type unwrapping) -- tuple/struct/slice destructuring patterns bind nothing this wave, a documented gap proven by a dedicated test, not a silent omission. Only Expr::Assign with a single-segment Expr::Path LHS produces a Store; compound assignment (`x += 1`) parses as Expr::Binary in this syn version (independently confirmed by the verification pass via a throwaway parse probe), so its operands are ordinary Uses.
data_flow_model.scope_this_wave: No alias/borrow/points-to analysis: references, compound places (self.field, arr[i], *ptr), and cross-function value flow are not modeled -- reads as Unresolved or simply not emitted as Store/Definition. Closures get no data-flow scoping of their own (consistent with R4.6's CFG giving closures no CFG either -- neither has a FunctionIdentity to attribute records to). Every omission is Unresolved or absent by design, never fabricated -- independently confirmed true of the code by direct read, not just doc-comment assertion.
data_flow_model.graph_projection: core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs: the previously no-op SemanticObservation::DataFlow arm now creates one Value node per observation (role/resolution/is_parameter/is_return_flow attributes) plus an unconditional HAS_VALUE edge from the owning function's FunctionIdentity node (present for every value event, mirroring R4.6's HAS_BLOCK), and a RESOLVES_TO edge from a Use/Store's node to its resolved Definition's node only when resolved_definition is Some. An Unresolved value correctly produces no dangling or fabricated edge -- confirmed by a dedicated test and independently falsified (making the edge unconditional broke exactly the two tests that depend on the guard).

bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_wave.summary: is_return_flow was computed structurally per-block (a block's own last bare-identifier statement was unconditionally flagged as return-flow if it looked like a tail expression), so a non-tail nested block -- e.g. the branches of `let y = if cond { x } else { x };` -- was silently over-flagged as the function's return value even though its value only feeds a local `let` binding.
bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_wave.discovered_by: independent verification pass, via direct code-read of walk_block/walk_expr plus a reverted probe test, contradicting the field's own doc comment (which the initial 12-test corpus never exercised: no non-tail nested if/block fixture existed).
bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_wave.severity_at_discovery: non-blocking for record identity, resolution, or graph structure -- is_return_flow is excluded from identity_key() and not consumed by the RESOLVES_TO edge logic -- but a real, silent contradiction of the field's documented contract.
bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_wave.fix_mechanism: walk_block now takes the caller's own is_return_flow context instead of recomputing it structurally from each block's own shape; a tail statement only propagates return-flow when the block itself is in that context. Loop/while/for bodies now explicitly pass false (never return-flow); the function's own top-level body passes true; Expr::Block and Expr::If's then_branch now thread the context they were given instead of ignoring it.
bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_wave.regression_coverage: new fixture `if_in_let` + test `return_flow_does_not_leak_out_of_a_non_tail_if_branch`: asserts all three `x` uses inside `let y = if x > 0 { x } else { x };` are NOT return-flow, while the function's own bare-identifier tail `y` is.
bug_found_and_fixed_during_this_wave.real_evidence_before_after: self-systemize against this repository's own source: is_return_flow=true count dropped from 41 (buggy) to 38 (fixed) -- consistent with removing exactly the false positives, not a wholesale behavior change (7172 -> 7190 total DataFlow records between runs reflects incidental source drift from the fix commit itself, not the bug).

pipeline_losslessness.batch_to_census: build_census() required zero code changes to carry DataFlow observations losslessly -- it operates generically over SemanticObservation, exactly as it did for R4.5/R4.6.
pipeline_losslessness.census_to_normalization: normalize()/normalize_typed_records() likewise required zero code changes; confirmed by a dedicated runtime multi-extractor round-trip test.
pipeline_losslessness.normalization_to_graph: add_typed_semantic_nodes()'s DataFlow arm is the one place that DID require new code this wave (previously part of a combined no-op arm) -- Value node + HAS_VALUE edge + conditional RESOLVES_TO edge, proven by three dedicated graph tests.

multi_extractor_proof.claim: Two independent extractors reporting the identical DataFlow value claim (same repository/revision/function/name/span/role) both survive Census and Normalization as two independent typed_semantic_records entries.
multi_extractor_proof.mechanism: record_id() (built from ValueIdentity::identity_key(), which excludes resolution/resolved_definition/is_parameter/is_return_flow) is identical for both observations, proving the semantic CLAIM identity is unaffected by which extractor reported it; raw_observation_id() (extractor id/version + status + evidence_refs + provenance + full typed payload) differs between the two, so R4.3.3's raw_observation_id-keyed dedup (unmodified this wave) correctly keeps both.
